newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise, seen flat in wait for KGHM.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise, seen flat in wait for KGHM.

text.p: Polish shares rose slightly for the second session running and analysts saw the market flat or easing on Monday as investors save up for copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz SA's public offering starting on June 30.

"After the big success of the Bank Handlowy offer, demand for KGHM could be at least as big and...perhaps investors will refrain from buying on the bourse, leading to a flat trend," said Pawel Tarnowski Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.
Bank Handlowy, news of whose privatisation-offer oversubscription came on Wednesday, starts trade on the Warsaw bourse on June 26 or 30.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.3 percent to 16,048.1 points and turnover fell 6.5 percent to 128.6 million zlotys ($36.7 million) on all three markets. Gainers led losers by 58 to 32 with 16 stocks flat.
Analysts said Poland's good macroeconomic environment and hopes that money from the Handlowy oversubscription would flow to listed stocks should prevent steep falls.

They said this latter phenomoneon could be reflected in industrial and trading firm Elektrim's five-percent rise on Friday in moderate trade, though the bourse's largest-cap stock saw stronger selling after fixing and fell in continuous trade.
